title: weight-decay-canary-controller-with-safety-traceback
author: Sofia Rivera
release_notes: Introduces a weight-decay based canary controller for gradual traffic shifts with an automated safety traceback that re-evaluates recent requests when rollbacks occur.
description: Motivation: We want safer, more predictable canary rollouts for model updates that (1) decay newly-introduced canary weights over time when signals are noisy, (2) provide deterministic criteria for an automated rollback, and (3) capture a short history of recent in-flight requests for post-rollback traceback and lightweight regression triage. This PR implements a Weight-Decay Canary Controller and an associated Safety Traceback subsystem for quick regression context on automated rollbacks. Design summary: - Weight-decay policy: new canary cohorts start with configured target weight but are subject to an exponential decay factor if health signals (latency, error rate, quality score regressions) exhibit high variance over a short window. Decay reduces surface area while preserving the ability to re-escalate when signals stabilize. Parameters are configurable per-rollout: initial_weight, decay_halflife_seconds, min_floor_weight, and reevaluate_interval_seconds. - Safety Traceback: on a rollback event the controller snapshots a lightweight indexed summary of recent requests routed to the canary (request id, short prompt hash, model variant id, timestamp, top-3 metrics) for the trailing window. The indexed summary is stored in the customer tenant's ephemeral bucket (7-day TTL) and surfaced in the Console rollback UI with a one-click export for offline repro. - Decision logic: combines smoothed metrics (EWMA) and a small multi-metric gate (latency P95, error ratio, quality regression score) with configurable thresholds and hysteresis. When a gate trips, controller will either decay weight or issue a full rollback depending on severity. - Observability and audit: every decision emits a structured event (rollout.event) containing current weights, EWMA vectors, and traceback snapshot id. Implementation notes: - Controller is implemented as a new controller module under rollout/weight_decay_controller.go with a clean interface to the existing orchestration agent. - Added a lightweight in-memory circular buffer per canary shard that periodically flushes compacted indices to object storage (s3/GCS-compatible) with strict tenant ACLs. - Compat layer included so legacy rollout specs without decay settings default to no-decay behavior. - Added e2e and unit tests for decay math, gate trip/recovery, and traceback snapshot TTL enforcement. Commits summary: - feat(controller): initial weight-decay controller and policy enforcement (S. Rivera) - feat(traceback): snapshot indexer and storage adapter (S. Rivera) - test: unit tests for EWMA math and gate logic (J. Chen) - docs: rollout spec examples and console UI note (A. Patel) - ci: add integration job to emulate noisy signals and automated rollback path (M. Li) Files changed (high-level): - rollout/weight_decay_controller.go (new) - rollout/decay_policy_test.go (new) - orchestration/agent_integration.go (minor hooks) - storage/traceback_indexer.go (new) - storage/traceback_adapter_s3.go (new) - console/rollback_ui_patch.md (docs) - examples/rollouts/weight_decay_canary.yaml (examples) - ci/integration/noisy-rollout.yaml (ci job) Testing and CI: - Integration job simulates a canary with synthetic quality degradations and intermittent latency spikes. - CI runs include unit, integration and lint jobs. First run flagged a flaky integration test due to timing assumptions; adjusted reevaluate_interval_seconds and added deterministic clock in tests. Final CI status: pass. Review conversation (selected excerpts): - Amir Patel (reviewer): "Good overall design. Can we ensure the traceback snapshots do not leak PII? Add strict redaction hooks and document ACL model." - Sofia Rivera (author): "Added redaction hooks to the snapshot pipeline; snapshots are hashed and only short prompt prefixes are stored by default (configurable). Also added tenant-scoped storage paths and a small audit marker event." - Jia Chen (reviewer): "The decay math looks right but we should warn users in docs about brittle configs for very small canaries. Also requested explicit test for min_floor_weight behavior." - Sofia Rivera: "Added min_floor_weight unit test and docs note in examples/rollouts/weight_decay_canary.yaml." - Marcus Li (SRE): "Integration job revealed even small background jitter can trigger decay too quickly; suggest a default halflife of 30s for short-rollouts and 5m for long ones. We should expose presets in Console." - Sofia Rivera: "Added preset profiles and Console hint text; defaults chosen after perf lab experiments." - QA: "Observed a rare race in buffer flush during tenant shutdown." - Sofia Rivera: "Fixed by adding a graceful drain hook and retry-on-failure for final flush." Risk and mitigations: - Storage cost: snapshots are compact and TTL'd to 7 days by default; customers can opt-out or set shorter TTLs. - Privacy: prompt text is hashed with configurable prefix length and a redaction hook allows teams to supply custom scrubbers. - Performance: circular buffer is bounded and uses async flush to avoid adding tail latency. Benchmarks: - Throughput impact: microbench in perf-lab shows <0.7% median latency increase at 95th percentile for 8-CPU shards and <1.2% for 16-CPU shards under heavy concurrency. - Storage footprint: default settings produce ~120KB/day per active canary. Backwards compatibility: - Existing rollout specs continue to work; decay behavior only engages for rollouts that provide a decay policy. Operational: - Console: new Rollout -> Weight-decay canary view with realtime weight graph and rollback button wired to traceback export. - Admin API: new endpoints to list snapshot ids for a tenant and to fetch exported CSVs (RBAC-protected). Merge notes: - Squashed into a single commit; feature gated behind rollout.experimental.weight_decay flag. - Added migration note: no persistent DB schema changes required. - Deployed to staging and validated against perf-lab workloads. Follow-ups: - ENG-2055: Add opt-in encrypted HSM storage for traceback indices for regulated customers. - ENG-2060: Provide automated replay harness that can re-run top-N snapshots against candidate models for quick regression repro. Overall this PR delivers a pragmatic, configurable canary decay capability with a pragmatic safety traceback mechanism to speed up rollback triage and reduce MTTR for regression incidents.
